notes.author: agent:claude
notes.text: Admin-channel recommendation pending owner confirmation: a Unix domain socket in the 0700 app data directory with 0600 permissions, as used by Docker, tailscaled and containerd. Stage 1 stores only the token verifier, so the CLI can no longer read the raw secret from a 0600 service-access file and call loopback HTTP as it does today. OS file permissions become the authority. Linux and macOS are the supported platforms; Windows is out of scope.

problem: Runtime, MCP and knowledge currently use separate credential paths. The owner needs one CLI-selected installation mode and one generated token covering all functions, without a second knowledge login.

risk.rollback: Preserve data and historical identities. Reject an invalid target mode before changing the active policy. Recover through local CLI into token mode with a newly emitted credential; never silently fall back to open or stop managed processes to repair authentication.

scope: Implement stage 1 of NOTE-20260909-self-hosted-saas-plan/authentication-modes-and-plugin.md: one persisted installation-wide open, token or better-auth setting controlled by local administrator CLI.

Open mode requires no authentication for any enabled Web/API/MCP/knowledge flow, including writes, approvals, attachments and export/import. Record anonymous installation authority honestly; preserve validation, process ownership, reservations and origin protections. Explicit CLI selection is sufficient; do not add a password, token, TLS prerequisite or confirmation gate for open mode.

Token mode uses one CLI-generated installation credential across runtime, knowledge and all functions exposed by each transport. A browser session may derive from that credential, but no separate knowledge credential or grant setup is required for the installation owner. Keep optional scoped agent credentials limited to their grants.

Add CLI status, mode selection, token generation and explicit rotation through shared operations. Online configuration uses an OS-protected local administrative channel; offline access retains the controller singleton lock. Mode changes are not exposed through anonymous HTTP or MCP tools.

Store only the token verifier, emit the secret through private CLI output, retain it across controller restarts and invalidate derived sessions on rotation. Define service-open and config-mcp behavior without hidden credential generation or leaking secrets in arguments/logs.

Unify caller context across HTTP/MCP/CLI, SSE, identity administration and knowledge. Migrate existing pairing, MCP and knowledge credentials explicitly without silently expanding old token privileges or rewriting historical identities.

Expose better-auth as an unavailable provider in stage 1: stable auth_provider_unavailable error and to-be-implemented message, unchanged active mode. A configured provider missing at startup fails before exposing operations, with no fallback to open.

Validate and apply mode transitions atomically; invalidate old browser/MCP sessions and subscriptions without restarting managed project servers or losing existing reservation semantics. New installs default to token and existing installs remain protected until explicit migration.
source: Owner authentication roadmap decision on 2026-09-17; supersedes independent Web/MCP switches
title: Configure global open, token and Better Auth modes from CLI
trigger: Owner requested this as authentication roadmap stage 1 on 2026-09-17; stage 2 Better Auth depends on its shared provider boundary.
validation: Run the complete HTTP/MCP/CLI/browser matrix in open and token modes, including runtime, test admission, existing/new knowledge projects, approvals, attachments, export/import, identity administration and SSE. Token mode must need only one installation credential; open mode must need none.
Verify missing/wrong/rotated tokens fail in token mode, restarts preserve the token, generation does not implicitly rotate, and rotation invalidates all derived sessions and existing subscriptions.

Verify anonymous operations and shared-token operations do not falsely identify a particular human; retain historical IDs, records and grants. Existing scoped tokens do not inherit installation-token privileges.
Verify unsupported better-auth selection leaves the active mode unchanged, manually configured missing providers fail closed, and no configuration failure selects open.
Verify online/offline CLI administration respects OS authority and singleton ownership, anonymous requests cannot change modes, and MCP cannot mint credentials or bypass its tool/claim rules.
Verify migration of service access and client configuration, secret-free diagnostics, browser flows, pnpm check, build and packaged installation according to repository verification rules.
value: One explicit installation policy removes repeated knowledge authentication and keeps a complete MIT self-hosted edition while establishing the optional provider boundary.
